title: v2.10.0-beta.2: ECH with domains that use wildcard certificates not work

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I'm not able to reproduce this with essentially the same setup: registered domain as the ECH domain, and a wildcard subdomain for all the sites under it, and using `prefer_wildcard: true`.

In Firefox, I'm able to successfully connect to any subdomain with ECH as expected. (Verified with Wireshark a minute ago.)

I'm not sure if you've reset your Caddy data dir at all, or at least the `ech` directory (you can keep the certs and other data), but that might be worth a try since I know you've been troubleshooting a few ECH issues already; adjust this path accordingly: `rm -rf $HOME/.local/share/caddy/ech`

Caddy keeps track of where it has published ECH information to, so it doesn't constantly republish at every config load. But it doesn't always keep that in sync (again, for efficiency reasons), so you may want to clear that ech folder so Caddy will republish everything.

I am not sure why prefer_wildcard has any impact on ECH... I am not experiencing the same behavior when I toggle it on or off.

Does it work with Firefox? (Enable DNS-over-HTTPS in Settings, and then use Wireshark to confirm.)

comments.body:
@reporter Thanks, there's quite a bit going on... breaking this down.

> Here had other people reproduced that domains use wildcard cert ECH unwork, with a different local environments and ISP. the log: https://paste.rs/EZqJA

I think that's expected, right? It's using the wildcard certificate because `prefer_wildcards` is false, and "requested but no ECHConfig available" is probably showing because there aren't any HTTPS records for that domain:

```
$ doggo -t HTTPS matrix.nyaw.xyz
NAME	TYPE	CLASS	TTL	ADDRESS	NAMESERVER 


```

> After removing the s3-certmagic part in my config, and clean caddy state directory on filesystem: ... But the domains' ech working status remains the same (domain use wildcard cert, ech doesn't work).

I would love to see the _full_ logs for this, along with the curl request, for this specific test. I am unable to reproduce the behavior here. If the site's specific cert is loaded, Caddy uses it. Otherwise it uses the wildcard.

> Then clean the caddy state directory on filesystem and all HTTPS record on cloudflare, restart caddy, This time it doesn't even adds any HTTPS record to cloudflare for ech..(I've waiting for it for minutes.)

That's because the metadata file in storage already indicated it was published: `{"level":"debug","ts":1741855914.6403925,"logger":"tls.ech","msg":"ECH config list already published by publisher for associated domains","config_ids":[53],"publisher":"dns.providers.cloudflare"}`

So, it must be that storage wasn't cleared as you say.

I think we just need to be very very precise when troubleshooting; once the HTTPS record is published, Caddy won't expect it to disappear like that, unless its state regarding publishing the record also disappears. (Again, for efficiency: it would not be a good idea to hit DNS provider APIs every config load, since some users load configs multiple times per minute.)

comments.body:
> Not in every test, but test in OS/browsers that not ever accessed the domains before show the same result. And while testing with browser I always newly start one.

In my experience, restarting the browser isn't enough. DNS is very persnickety and sticky. 🙂 

> BTW have you ever tested with curl?

I normally do test exclusively with curl or with Go programs, but in this case, I haven't; mainly because getting curl with ECH up and running on my platform was too complicated for the time I had.

>  I would like to first rule out discrepancies in test results caused by differences in clients, even though the test results on the browser appear negative to me.

Fair point, and I would like to also, since I typically strongly advise _against_ using browsers for testing, because they do all sorts of funky magic. And given the experimental nature of the tech, it's quite possible that clients differ significantly, or have bugs.

If I have time to get curl with ECH running, I will try it; but until then, it's still imperative that _every_ test starts with a clean slate in every relevant way: DNS cache, TLS session, TCP connection, restarting the server process, recompiling the server binary, etc etc. (I've had to be very careful about that in development as well. Yes I'm sure there are easier ways, and yes I'm stubborn. 😉)

Been a bit sidetracked with some other pressing issues, but I'm returning to this one ASAP (right after the weekend, I hope). In the meantime if you make any progress, keep me posted!

@reporter Well, I find your case a bit perplexing, but I still have a hunch it may be due to conflations of state. i.e. I would be curious if, now that your rate limit blocks have passed, you could try again with the latest beta (2.10 beta 3) which just finished releasing.

Nothing in it *should* fix your issue directly, but I'm still curious to try it, especially with a completely clean slate:

- Clear the `ech` subfolder ONLY of the Caddy data directory (keep your certificates). I recommend NOT using S3 storage for testing (or at all, really).
- Ensure existing HTTPS records have been cleared from DNS.
- Ensure your browser or client/system DNS cache is cleared. Prefer Firefox and, I suppose curl, since I believe their ECH implementations are most functional at the moment. I am not really interested in debugging third party clients at the moment, just our server.
- Ensure your config is correct (and minimal).
- Preserve Caddy logs, actual config used, and actual command that Caddy was started with.
